```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
has_highs <- requireNamespace("highs", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(multimod)
mod <- example_models$energyRt$multimod
mod
```

A framework model such as energyRt declares each parameter over every
dimension it may vary by (technology, commodity, region, year, timeslice) and
carries equations for features a given scenario may not use. Two
transformations remove the resulting redundancy without changing the
optimum:

1. **Folding** drops a dimension from a parameter whose values are constant
   across it (data redundancy).
2. **Trimming** flags sets, parameters, mappings, variables and equations
   with no data or no instances (structural redundancy).

Both are reversible, and both are honoured by the MathProg, JuMP, Pyomo and
LaTeX writers and by the matrix route.

## Folding

A parameter with the same value in every timeslice is stored once per
remaining index combination, and the equations that use it lose the folded
index:

```
# before
vTechInp[t,c,r,y,s] >= pTechCinp2use[t,c,r,y,s] * vTechAct[t,r,y,s]
# after
vTechInp[t,c,r,y,s] >= pTechCinp2use[t,c,r,y]   * vTechAct[t,r,y,s]
```

### Redundancy in the data

`analyze_parameter_redundancy()` counts, per parameter, the rows that repeat
a value.

```{r redundancy}
red <- analyze_parameter_redundancy(mod, verbose = FALSE)
red <- red[order(-red$orig_redundancy_pct), ]
knitr::kable(
  head(red[, c("param_name", "dims", "orig_rows", "orig_unique",
               "orig_redundancy_pct")], 8),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Parameters with the most repeated values (rows; redundancy in %)"
)
```

### Fold specification

`create_fold_spec()` takes one entry per dimension to fold, naming the
*validation mappings* that state which entities may vary by that dimension;
a parameter folds only when its values are constant within every group the
mapping allows. In energyRt these are `mTechTimeslice` for technologies and
`mCommTimeslice` for commodities.

```{r fold-spec}
fold_spec <- create_fold_spec(
  mod,
  fold_dims = list(
    timeslice = list(tech = "mTechTimeslice", comm = "mCommTimeslice")
  ),
  verbose = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  head(fold_spec[, c("param_name", "validation_mapping", "can_fold", "unproven")], 8),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Fold specification, first rows"
)
```

`unproven` marks parameters without a validation mapping for their entity
type. Several dimensions are folded in the order given:

```{r fold-spec-multi, eval = FALSE}
create_fold_spec(
  mod,
  fold_dims = list(
    timeslice = list(tech = "mTechTimeslice", comm = "mCommTimeslice"),
    region    = list(comm = "mCommRegion")
  )
)
```

### Fold and unfold

```{r fold}
mod_folded <- fold_model(mod, fold_spec = fold_spec, verbose = FALSE)
c(original = is_folded(mod), folded = is_folded(mod_folded))
fs <- get_fold_summary(mod_folded, format = "data.frame")
knitr::kable(
  fs[, c("parameter", "removed_dims", "original_rows", "folded_rows", "compression")],
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Folded parameters (rows; compression = original / folded rows)"
)
```

A folded parameter keeps its declared dimensions in `$dims`;
`get_active_dims()` returns the ones in force.

```{r active-dims}
p <- mod_folded$parameters$pTechCinp2use
p$dims
get_active_dims(p)
```

`unfold_model()` restores the original data:

```{r unfold}
mod_unfolded <- unfold_model(mod_folded, verbose = FALSE)
c(original = nrow(mod$parameters$pTechCinp2use$data),
  unfolded = nrow(mod_unfolded$parameters$pTechCinp2use$data))
```

## Trimming

Trimming flags with `$trimmed = TRUE`, and deletes nothing:

- sets, parameters and mappings without data;
- variables over an empty domain;
- equations with an empty domain or only trimmed variables.

Anything a remaining equation still uses is then unflagged, so no element a
surviving equation needs is trimmed. Folding comes first, since it can empty
a parameter.

```{r trim}
mod_trimmed <- trim_model(mod_folded, verbose = FALSE)
knitr::kable(
  get_trim_summary(mod_trimmed, format = "data.frame"),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "Elements trimmed, by type (counts)"
)
```

`is_trimmed()` applies to a model or to one element; `untrim_model()` clears
the flags.

```{r trim-elements}
trimmed_eqs <- get_trim_summary(mod_trimmed, format = "list")$equations$names
head(trimmed_eqs)
is_trimmed(mod_trimmed$equations$eqTechGrp2Sng)
is_trimmed(mod_trimmed$equations$eqTechCap)
is_trimmed(untrim_model(mod_trimmed))
```

## Folding and trimming compared

| | Folding | Trimming |
|---|---|---|
| Targets | data redundancy | structural redundancy |
| Mechanism | collapses a constant dimension | flags unused elements |
| Reduces | parameter rows, coefficients | sets, parameters, variables, equations emitted |
| Needs | validation mappings | nothing; driven by the data |
| Reversed by | `unfold_model()` | `untrim_model()` |

## Writing a reduced model

`write_gmpl()`, `write_jump()` and `write_pyomo()` use the folded dimensions
and skip trimmed elements; `write_latex()` shows the reduced model, or the
full one with the removed parts marked (`model_view = "full"`);
`model_to_lp()` builds the matrix from the active dimensions.

```{r write, eval = FALSE}
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "trimmed")
save_model(mod_trimmed, dir, format = "csv")
write_gmpl(mod_trimmed, model_dir = dir)
write_jump(mod_trimmed, model_dir = dir)
```

A fold specification is a data frame; saved with `saveRDS()`, it applies to
other scenarios of the same model.

## Limitations

- A parameter folds only when every group is constant across the dimension.
- Folding needs validation mappings; for a model other than energyRt, the
  specification names them.
- Folding holds the parameter data in memory while it runs.
- Trimming only flags elements; their data stays in the model and on disk.

## The optimum is unchanged

```{r verify, eval = has_highs}
r0 <- solve_highs(mod, attach = FALSE)
r1 <- solve_highs(mod_folded, attach = FALSE)
r2 <- solve_highs(mod_trimmed, attach = FALSE)
c(original = r0$objective, folded = r1$objective, trimmed = r2$objective)
```
